title: refactor: share request logging and embedding response shaping
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Rebuilds only the remaining request-logger and embedding-response deduplication from #12042 on current main.
- Shares Gen/Enter request context, timing, and environment-based logging while preserving Gen URL redaction and Enter's existing URL formatting; existing middleware imports and LoggerVariables exports remain compatible.
- Shares sorting and float/base64 shaping for Azure OpenAI, Cohere, and Fireworks; keeps provider calls, validation, usage headers, and billing unchanged.
- Adds eight logger cases and three batched base64/billing cases; existing provider fixtures now return reversed entries to exercise sorting. Validated 84 Gen tests, 16 Enter tests, both service typechecks, Biome, and whitespace checks.
- Leaves unrelated constants/header micro-extractions and behavior changes from #12042 out of scope; auth metadata consolidation already landed in #12924.

gist.headline: One logger, two hives
gist.blurb: Gen and Enter now share the same request-logging roots, while embeddings get one careful response-shaping path. The plumbing is less duplicated; the API keeps behaving exactly as it did.
gist.summary: Shared Gen/Enter request context, timing, and environment-based logging in a common middleware module, and centralized embedding sorting plus float/base64 response shaping for Azure OpenAI, Cohere, and Fireworks without changing provider calls, validation, usage headers, or billing.
gist.impact: Developers get consistent internal logging and embedding-response ordering across providers while Gen URL redaction, Enter URL formatting, billing, and existing middleware imports remain intact.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy shared garden-shed logging station represents one middleware root feeding both Gen and Enter paths: Polli tidies two labeled watering hoses into a single glowing logbook, while sorted embedding crystals move neatly into matching jars. A retro terminal, code-plants, and small provider-colored-but-pastel jars convey response shaping and preserved order without implying a user-visible API change.
